description: LunarSafe is a team focused on exploring innovative solutions for safer and smarter lunar exploration. Our project aims to assess potential Moon South Pole landing sites using NASA datasets, focusing on lunar terrain, sunlight availability, and potential water-ice resources. We aim to transform scientific data into meaningful insights that can support future lunar missions and sustainable space exploration.
summary: LunarSafe is a proposed data-driven solution designed to assess and compare potential landing sites near the Moon's South Pole. The project aims to use publicly available NASA lunar datasets to evaluate important factors such as surface terrain, slope, sunlight availability, and proximity to permanently shadowed regions that may contain water ice. By combining these indicators into an easy-to-understand comparison framework, LunarSafe seeks to help students, researchers, and future mission planners explore potential landing regions more effectively. The project supports safer, smarter, and more sustainable lunar exploration by making scientific information easier to understand and analyze.
details:
Project Overview

LunarSafe is a proposed data-driven solution designed to assess and compare potential landing regions near the Moon's South Pole using publicly available NASA lunar science datasets.

How It Works

The proposed framework evaluates important factors, including lunar surface terrain, slope conditions, sunlight availability, and proximity to permanently shadowed regions. It organizes these indicators into an understandable comparison framework to help users explore potential landing regions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LunarSafe aims to make lunar scientific information more accessible and understandable. It supports educational research, encourages data-driven exploration, and promotes awareness of the challenges associated with future lunar missions.

Data Sources

The project plans to use publicly available resources from NASA, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) data and the NASA Planetary Data System.

Tools and Technologies

The proposed workflow may use QGIS for geospatial data exploration, spreadsheet software for data organization, and visualization tools for presenting comparisons. These tools should only be listed as used technologies after they have actually been used.

Innovation and Creativity

LunarSafe brings multiple lunar exploration indicators together in one transparent assessment concept. It emphasizes understandable comparisons, scientific evidence, and data limitations rather than relying on unsupported landing-site safety claims.

Future Scope

Future development may include an interactive lunar map, automated data processing, advanced terrain analysis, and additional NASA datasets to support more detailed lunar exploration research.
